name: Sumava National Park
blurb: Spruce forest, bark beetles and the returned lynx of the Bohemian Forest.

tip.title: Remove the lynx
tip.text: Lynx hunt roe deer, red deer and foxes. Set Eurasian lynx to -100% and watch roe deer, then the bilberry and young trees they browse.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Light reaching the forest floor limits the growth of berries, seedlings and mountain meadows beneath the canopy.
Break down fallen leaves, beetle-killed spruce and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
Dominant conifer of the Bohemian Forest, widely planted. Spruce stands stressed by wind or drought are the main host of the spruce bark beetle.
A broadleaf tree of the lower and middle slopes. Its nuts feed wild boar and rodents.
A small tree whose berries are eaten by foxes, martens and many birds.
Low shrub of the forest floor. Its leaves and berries feed deer, and martens take the fruit.

nodes.name: Eurasian spruce bark beetle
nodes.desc: Breeds under spruce bark and can overwhelm stressed trees in outbreaks, a major natural disturbance in Sumava.
A small browsing deer that eats leaves, shoots and berries of trees and shrubs; the preferred prey of lynx where common.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: The largest deer of the forest. It grazes grasses, browses shrubs such as bilberry and is prey for wolves and lynx.
Omnivore that roots for nuts, plants, small animals and carrion in the forest.
A forest rodent that eats seeds and small invertebrates; prey for foxes, martens and buzzards.
Splits bark to reach insect larvae, so it can help limit bark beetle numbers.
Adaptable predator and scavenger that eats rodents, birds, carrion and fruit.
Hawk that hunts rodents and other small animals over forest edges and clearings.
Large crow that scavenges carcasses, such as those left by lynx and wolves.
Ambush hunter, mainly of roe deer. Wiped out in Bohemia in the 1800s, it was reintroduced to the Sumava area in the 1980s.
Pack hunter of deer and wild boar, recorded near Sumava; leaves carcasses that scavengers use.

story: Sumava National Park is a forest located in Czechia in the South Bohemian regions along the border with Germany and Austria. It protects a little-inhabited mountain range covered by extensive forest and raised peat bogs. Since the 1970s, the park has sheltered a stable population of lynxes.
matters: The park preserves the most extensive forest in Central Europe and features a mosaic of habitats like glacial lakes and primeval forest remnants that are little disturbed by human activity.
